forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Wiltshire faces £86m schools funding deficit waiting for government approval
news_drafts.lead: Wiltshire Council's plan to balance its special needs education budget depends on approval from the Department for Education that has not yet come through. The council is holding a cumulative deficit of £86.384m in its dedicated schools grant, the government funding that pays for schools, and can only access a grant covering 90 per cent of it if ministers approve its reform plan. The council expects to hear in September or October whether the plan has been approved. The pressures driving the deficit are intensifying: the number of children with education and care plans has grown 72 per cent in five years, from 4,158 to 7,149, and more of them have complex needs. Demand for specialist school places has outpaced the council's capital plans, which are now nearly fully committed with almost no budget buffer. If the Department for Education rejects the plan, the council would face the full £86.384m exposure, which it warns could force "difficult decisions about resources across the organisation".

findings.paper_title: Stone Circle Governance - Audit and Governance Committee Biannual Report October 2026
findings.headline: Work underway to review Stone Circle loans and update documentation to reflect current borrowing arrangements
findings.detail: The Council and Stone Circle companies are working to review existing loan arrangements and update documentation to reflect current borrowing status. A wider review of loan consolidation, repayment obligations and interest management is being prepared.
findings.matters: Loan review and consolidation planning shows the Council is actively managing its debt exposure to the companies
findings.quote: Work is underway between the companies and Council officers to review the loans and update documentation to reflect current borrowing arrangements. A wider review of consolidation, repayment and interest management is also to be prepared.

findings.paper_title: Stone Circle Governance - Audit and Governance Committee Biannual Report October 2026
findings.headline: Stone Circle Audit and Risk Committee established March 2026 with independent members to strengthen governance assurance
findings.detail: A dedicated Stone Circle Audit and Risk Committee was established in March 2026 to provide independent scrutiny of financial reporting, audit, risk management, internal control and governance matters at group level. The committee comprises an independent chair, council representative and external independent member.
findings.matters: Establishment of dedicated audit and risk oversight committee strengthens governance framework and provides additional assurance to stakeholders
findings.quote: The Stone Circle Audit and Risk Committee was established in March 2026. The Committee comprises Shane Egan as Chair, Deborah Bull as the Council representative and Gregory Cain as an independent member. The Committee held its first meeting in May 2026 and met again in August 2026.

findings.paper_title: Stone Circle Governance - Audit and Governance Committee Biannual Report October 2026
findings.headline: Outstanding internal audit actions relating to emergency decision-making and procurement governance remain under review
findings.detail: Internal audit recommendations in relation to emergency decision-making and procurement governance have not yet been fully closed. The Scheme of Delegation and the companies' procurement procedures are currently being reviewed and will be reported through the Audit and Risk Committee's work programme.
findings.matters: Unresolved audit recommendations indicate control gaps that could affect financial management and governance
findings.quote: Outstanding internal audit actions relating to emergency decision-making and procurement governance remain under review. The Scheme of Delegation and the companies' procurement procedures are to be reported through the Audit and Risk Committee work programme.

findings.paper_title: Stone Circle Governance - Audit and Governance Committee Biannual Report October 2026
findings.headline: No material issues and no significant deficiencies in internal control identified in 2025/26 external audit
findings.detail: External auditors reviewed the Stone Circle companies' financial statements and control environment for the year ended 31 March 2026. No material issues were identified and no significant deficiencies in internal control were found during the audit.
findings.matters: Clean audit findings provide assurance that financial reporting and internal controls are effective
findings.quote: The external auditors reported that no material issues and no significant deficiencies in internal control had been identified during the 2025/26 audit.

findings.paper_title: Stone Circle Governance - Audit and Governance Committee Biannual Report October 2026
findings.headline: Housing Company achieved 90.3% occupancy with 41 keyworker households completed
findings.detail: The Housing Company's September 2026 update reported improved occupancy at 90.3% with a reduction in empty homes. The company continues to make progress with its keyworker housing offer, with 41 keyworker households completed at the time of the report.
findings.matters: Occupancy levels and let-up rates directly determine rental income available to service debt and recover Development Company losses
findings.quote: Its September 2026 update reported improved occupancy (90.3%) and a reduction in empty homes, progress with the keyworker housing offer, with 41 keyworker households completed at the time of the report
